chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khash'ami, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the absconding Muslim slave: he is returned to the Muslim.
And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who seized an absconding slave, so he absconded from him: he said, there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الآبِق: The absconding slave who runs away from his master
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: There is nothing upon him (no penalty/compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an absconding Muslim slave and the person who captures him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the fiqh of al-ābiq (the absconding slave), affirming the master's right to reclaim the slave while clarifying that a third party who captures him bears no liability if the slave subsequently escapes. This ruling reflects the pre-modern Islamic legal context where slavery was regulated by specific property laws, ensuring that temporary possession did not create permanent financial obligation for the captor. It underscores the principle of risk allocation in commercial and social transactions within Shia jurisprudence.
